llm.summary: This study skill is mostly aligned with exam-prep reminders, but it can create persistent QQ delivery jobs too broadly and one README command targets a fixed QQ recipient.

dimensions.detail: The script reads only bundled reference files and uses OpenClaw cron and qqbot capabilities; QUICKSTART troubleshooting also suggests a mutable global npm install of @openclaw/cli, which is broader than ideal but not evidence of malicious code.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: README.md includes a copy-paste cron creation example that says to replace the user's openid but actually contains a fixed QQ recipient value, creating a real risk of recurring messages going to the wrong account.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires cron setup whenever broad prep-related phrases are mentioned, including queries for chapter highlights or vocabulary, which can turn read-only study requests into persistent scheduled jobs without an explicit confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates recurring OpenClaw scheduler entries using payload.kind agentTurn with deliver=true to qqbot, and the mandatory trigger wording does not sufficiently limit persistence to explicit user-directed reminder setup.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose includes Chinese soft-exam study content, daily pushes, chapter lookup, vocabulary, and QQ bot delivery, so file reads, bundled study resources, and scheduled reminders are largely purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing. Only create the daily push job if you explicitly want recurring QQ messages, verify the QQ openid before running any README cron command, and check OpenClaw cron list afterward so you can delete unwanted jobs. Prefer the setup script over the README heredoc because the script prompts for your own openid.
llm.findings:
[T01] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: daily reminders are expected, but forcing cron creation for broad study requests is overbroad and can create persistence without clear user intent.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: README.md embeds a fixed QQ openid in an executable cron example despite surrounding text telling users to replace it.
[T08] expected: Downgraded to guidance: the unpinned global @openclaw/cli install appears only in troubleshooting and is a supply-chain hygiene issue, not evidence of bundled malicious behavior.
[TP4] expected: Partly downgraded: QQ delivery and daily push behavior are disclosed in the description and metadata, but the broad mandatory scheduler rule remains under-scoped.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for the forced scheduling path: scheduled delivery is part of the skill, but creating it from broad content requests is not adequately user-controlled.
[SDI-2] expected: Mostly expected: QQ channel delivery and openid routing fit the reminder purpose, though users should verify the recipient before creating a job.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a concern where broad triggers combine with persistence; generic study terms should not automatically create scheduled jobs.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: setup documents persistence, but the skill lacks a strong confirmation requirement before cron creation from runtime instructions.
[AS3] expected: Overridden: the cited ls command checks this skill's own installed SKILL.md path for troubleshooting and does not enumerate unrelated installed skills.
[E3] expected: Overridden: the cited filesystem checks are scoped to this skill's own files and reference directory, not credential or broad home-directory reconnaissance.
[AE4] expected: Overridden: inspected files are UTF-8 Chinese-language content and a hidden-control-character scan did not show suspicious bidi or zero-width markers.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-language content is coherent with a China-specific Chinese exam preparation skill, though documenting the intended audience would improve clarity.
[LP3] expected: Treated as a note: the skill declares qqbot config but does not clearly declare cron/tool scope; this matters mainly because the runtime instructions are overbroad.
